title: Frontend: Expense Tracker
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Expense Tracker. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App. Controlled Description and Cents inputs create expenses with Add[data-action=add]. Trim Description; require positive integer cents, otherwise show Invalid expense and create nothing. li[data-expense=ID] use sequential IDs starting 1 with Delete[data-delete=ID]. Output total cents in [data-testid=total].
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Store immutable expense records with stable IDs and validated amounts.
alternativeApproaches: Add multiple currencies with explicit conversion rates and avoid summing unlike monetary units.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Zero/negative policy; editing; deletion.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
